summary: Backend regression verification for the 'server not saved' fix in POST /api/data/status. Endpoint now uses get_current_user_allow_expired so a hit is ALWAYS persisted to db.hits regardless of plan state; forwarding is gated on has_access where is_admin = user.is_admin OR user.telegram_id == settings.ADMIN_TELEGRAM_ID (stale-flag safety). Added an admin-by-id fixture + test to cover the CARAXSS/owner scenario. All 12 pytest cases PASS (100%).
critical_code_review_comments: routes/data.py:submit_status now depends on get_current_user_allow_expired and inserts the hit BEFORE any forwarding decision — correctly decouples DB persistence from Telegram delivery. Fix directly addresses the reported 'server not saved' regression on expired/non-admin sessions.

is_admin = user.is_admin OR user.telegram_id == settings.ADMIN_TELEGRAM_ID is a good stale-flag safety net for the owner (@CARAXSS tid 5762701937). Verified via new test_admin_by_id_stale_flag_still_forwards.
should_forward = (is_charged or is_live) AND has_access — declines/dead/errors correctly return forwarded:false without dropping the DB insert.
Auth is still strictly enforced (missing bearer -> 401, revoked session -> 401). Ban check still runs in get_current_user_allow_expired.

Minor observation: charged_count increment in db.users.$inc runs even for expired non-admin users whose hit is NOT forwarded. That is likely intentional (owner still wants counters to reflect all activity) but flag for product review if not desired.

Minor observation: has_access does not consider the case where user.plan_expires_at is None for a non-admin (treated as no access, no forward). Current seed guarantees a value; if a future auth path leaves it None for legitimate plans this would silently drop forwarding — worth an explicit branch/log.
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/conftest.py (added admin_by_id_user fixture with backup+restore of any pre-existing ADMIN_TELEGRAM_ID user doc)
test_credentials: Seeded via tests/conftest.py: active tid=999000222, expired tid=999000111, admin (test) tid=999000333, revoked tid=999000444, and admin-by-id using the REAL settings.ADMIN_TELEGRAM_ID (5762701937 from backend/.env) with is_admin=false + expired plan. Any pre-existing doc for ADMIN_TELEGRAM_ID is snapshotted and restored at teardown; verified clean afterwards.
seed_data_creation: All ephemeral. teardown: db.users/sessions/hits deleted for tids 999000111/222/333/444; ADMIN_TELEGRAM_ID doc restored from snapshot (or deleted if it did not exist pre-test). Post-run DB check confirmed zero leftover test docs.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: `cd /app/backend && REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=http://localhost:8001 pytest tests/test_hit_pipeline.py -v`. 12 tests cover: (1) missing auth 401, (2) revoked session 401, (3) matching fp 200, (4) mismatched fp 200+persisted, (5) no fp header 200, (6) charged forwarded=true, (7) declined forwarded=false, (8) admin can list hits, (9) non-admin admin/hits -> 403, (10) EXPIRED non-admin -> 200 forwarded=false + persisted (NEW behavior, was 402 in iteration_1), (11) admin flag charged -> forwarded=true, (12) NEW: admin-by-id (telegram_id == ADMIN_TELEGRAM_ID) with stale is_admin=false + expired plan -> still forwarded=true. Telegram 'chat not found' warnings for fake tids are expected — assertions only check DB persistence + status + forwarded flag.
rca of the issue: Owner (@CARAXSS tid 5762701937) saw 'server not saved' because (a) POST /api/data/status used get_current_user which raises HTTPException(402, 'Access expired') BEFORE the db.hits.insert_one when the user's plan_expires_at was past, and (b) the stored is_admin flag on the owner's user doc was stale (False) after some earlier admin sync, so his own hits were treated as a plain expired user's hits — nothing persisted, nothing forwarded. Fix in routes/data.py:submit_status: switched dependency to get_current_user_allow_expired (so expired users still authenticate), moved has_access computation AFTER the insert path is unconditionally taken, and added telegram_id == settings.ADMIN_TELEGRAM_ID as an OR-clause to is_admin so the configured admin id is always treated as admin regardless of DB flag. Verified end-to-end: all 12 pytest assertions pass, including the new admin-by-id stale-flag case.
